logline: A poor Jeju girl and the boy who cherishes her find their lives braided across five decades of Korean modernity, from postwar privation through Seoul's restless growth, narrated by the daughter they raise together.

renewal.note: Single-season limited series, completed March 28, 2025. Creator has not indicated a continuation; the narrative resolves in 16 episodes.

bollymeter.basis: 100 percent Rotten Tomatoes from 9 critics, 9.1 IMDb rating, named by Time magazine as the best K-drama of 2025 and by South China Morning Post as one of the finest K-dramas of all time; Baeksang Best Drama win confirms the consensus.

pull_quotes.text: Sharply poignant; devastatingly tender; unfailingly warm. Understated, yet profoundly affecting.
A masterpiece that's well worth your time.

seasons.review_body: Released in four weekly volumes on Netflix from March 7 to 28, 2025, this 16-episode saga traces Ae-sun and Gwan-sik from 1950s Jeju through Seoul's boom years into old age. Critics converged on the same word: devastatingly. The 100-percent Rotten Tomatoes score from 9 reviewers noted a quality of tenderness rarely achieved by prestige K-drama, comparing it to Reply 1988 for cultural intimacy and surpassing it for emotional rigour. Time magazine named it the best Korean drama of 2025. The Baeksang Arts Awards swept four prizes including Best Drama. IU and Park Bo-gum as the young couple draw the consistent praise, while Moon So-ri and Park Hae-joon shoulder the middle-age chapters with equal authority. The audience score tracked critics at 98 percent Popcornmeter.

episode_reviews.title: Spring in a Heartbeat
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes Ae-sun in 1950s Jeju - poor, sharp, full of ambition she has no clear outlet for - and introduces the quietly devoted Gwan-sik. The period textures are meticulous and unhurried, and the episode sets an emotional register that critics described as making subsequent beats hit harder precisely because nothing is over-signalled here.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Ae-sun's first declaration of her impossible dream, delivered with casual certainty to someone who actually believes her.

episode_reviews.title: Life Goes On and On
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The midpoint of Volume II became the episode audiences cited most often as the one that broke them open. The rhythms of ordinary life - labour, small disappointments, unspoken devotion - accumulate into something audiences found almost unbearably moving. Critics who singled out specific episodes consistently mentioned this one as the emotional centre of the whole run.
episode_reviews.the_moment: A quiet domestic scene that reframes every sacrifice made in the earlier episodes without a single line of explicit dialogue.

episode_reviews.title: Here's to All You've Been Through
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale closes the full arc across five decades, returning to Jeju where the story began. Reviewers noted it does not reach for catharsis through event but through accumulation - the weight of a shared life made visible. The final image earned the show its reputation for restraint as a formal virtue.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The daughter's narration arriving full circle, giving retrospective meaning to what was always a love story about endurance as much as feeling.
